links.note: The old woman beside Valli chewing betel - the detail that made her repulsive to Valli, who refused her company.
What Valli tells the elderly woman when called a child - she insists she is not, which is the self-respect of 24214.
Valli telling the conductor to mind his own business while still amused - standing up for herself, which is 24214.
How the conductor addresses Valli - as Madam. Being treated properly rather than as a child is 24214.
The conductor addressing her as Madam - the respect Valli insists on.
Why the conductor calls Valli 'madam' - teasing her grown-up insistence on being treated as an adult.
Why the conductor refers to Valli as 'Madam' - her adult manner and her refusal to be treated as a child.
The one-way fare from village to town - thirty paise, half the sixty she had to save. 24215 names that sum.
What Valli paid for the round trip - sixty paise, the amount 24215 says she saved.
What she resisted on Village Fair Day - the merry-go-round, in order to save the fare.
How Valli saved for the journey and whether it was easy - resisting sweets, toys and the fair. That is 24215.
What Valli kept planning and calculating - the fare and how to put aside every stray coin.
Who was a real chatterbox - her aunt, whose chatter with her mother lets the trip pass unremarked. Part of keeping the plan hidden.
The aunt as the real chatterbox, talking with her mother while Valli's own secret stays unnoticed.
The next challenge after saving the money - to sneak out of the house. 24217 is the secrecy of the plan.
What Valli was planning to do - slip out for the bus ride while her mother slept, kept hidden from everyone.
Why Valli did not get off for sight-seeing - she stayed in the bus rather than risk her return fare. 24220 exactly.
Why she refused the stall and the drink - she would not spend money she needed to get home.
What saddened Valli - the dead cow. 24221 is that same cow, seen alive on the way out.
The dead cow that saddened her - the one she had laughed at earlier.
What amused Valli most - the cow running in front of the bus, the animal she later sees dead.
What made her laugh on the journey - the running cow, later found dead on the road.
What Valli saw on the way that made her laugh - the young cow galloping ahead of the bus.
Why Valli refuses to look out of the window on the way back - the dead cow has drained her delight. 24222 exactly.
What Valli means by 'things happening without our knowledge' - her own silent knowledge of the cow's death. The quiet change in her.
How the journey unfolds the mysteries of life and death for Valli - the encounter with death that changes her.
The incidents that present Valli as mature beyond her age - including her silence about the dead cow at the end.
Valli's greatest desire and how she fulfilled it - the whole arc from longing through planning to the journey, which is 24211.
What the text shows of the conductor - he was funny. The conductor is part of the bus world in 24219.
How we know the conductor was a good-natured jolly fellow - his jokes with Valli. Part of the bus and its people.
The speaking task on traffic and road safety following the bus journey - the bus and the road as the new world Valli enters.
